name: What the Case Manager and Team Decide
title: What the Case Manager and Team Decide
answer: In special education, the IEP team, including parents, holds the sole authority to decide eligibility, goals, services, and placement, and no AI tool may make those decisions. This matters because these choices shape a child's education for years, and AI output must remain only one input to a human-led process.

sections.body: This idea concerns the decisions that belong to the IEP team and case manager, which federal law reserves for the team and the parents. It addresses the risk that a drafted goal or a flagged eligibility could quietly become the decision if the team does not form its own view first. The problem is that when a machine makes the first call and a person is meant to check it, people tend to go along even with poor decisions. The team should therefore reach its own judgment before looking at any AI output. AI may assist, but the final word stays with the people who know the child.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school, the case manager and team decide eligibility, goals, services, and where a student is educated, while AI may help with supporting tasks listed in Figure 12.4. That list should be written into the district's human review rule from Chapter 3, so staff know which parts of the work are theirs alone. Case managers should feel free to set aside any AI suggestion that does not fit the student. Families must be real partners, since they know their child in ways no teacher or tool can and the law gives them the right to participate fully. The aim is more time for real conversation, not a faster meeting that presents decisions as already settled.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text applies the research on human review with full force here, noting that when a machine makes the first call and a person is supposed to check it, people tend to go along, even with poor decisions (Krugel et al., 2023). In special education, that risk means a drafted goal or a flagged eligibility could become the decision without real discussion. The text does not report a separate study of special education decisions themselves, so this idea rests on that human review finding together with established practice and law.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits are clear: no tool may make eligibility, goal, service, or placement decisions, because those belong to the IEP team and the parents under federal law. The risk is that AI output becomes the decision without genuine discussion, or that AI is used to speed through meetings or present decisions as settled, which undermines the family's right to participate fully. Case managers should feel free to set aside any AI suggestion that does not fit the student. The team should form its own view first and treat AI output as only one input. The final word always belongs to the people who know the child.
